items.definition: Tech noir (also called future noir or cyber-noir) fuses noir's hard keys, rain, and guilty blocking with science-fiction production design: screens, LEDs, and corporate towers as practical sources. Analog crime grammar sits inside a digital city.

items.name: Southern Gothic
items.prompt: Southern gothic air around [Subject], humid decay, Spanish moss dappled sun, late-afternoon gold gone sickly, porch tungsten, peeling paint. Name the heat and the house.
items.definition: Southern gothic cinematography uses the American South as a humid optical problem: late-afternoon gold gone sickly, Spanish-moss dappled light, porch tungsten, and haze that keeps heat in the air. Decay is on the walls. The threat is family, history, and something under the porch, not a city streetlamp.

items.name: Cosmic Horror
items.prompt: Cosmic horror framing of [Subject], scale wrong, geometry slightly illegal, under-lit face or a brightness that reveals too much, human irrelevance, extreme long shot or a corridor that does not vanish correctly. Do not prompt a gloved killer.
items.definition: Cosmic horror cinematography builds dread from human insignificance: extreme long shots, slightly illegal geometry, under-light on faces, and a brightness that reveals too much. The threat is not a man. Scale, entity, and knowledge that will not fit a face are the optical problem.

items.name: Vaporwave
items.prompt: Vaporwave treatment of [Subject], pink-cyan gradient, marble and palms, VHS bleed, centered 35mm, mall fluorescent fill, no hard unfilled cheek. Name the bust or the grid.
items.definition: The vaporwave aesthetic is a pastel, low-contrast look: pink-cyan gradients, marble and palms, mall fluorescents, and VHS chroma bleed, as if a 1980s future never shipped. The camera is often centered and still. There is no crime geometry unless you add it.

items.name: Documentary
items.prompt: Documentary look on [Subject], mixed color, unstyled wardrobe light, zoom finding focus, interview or observational coverage, respect without glamour. Name whether this is a sit-down or a follow.
items.definition: Documentary cinematography mixes observational coverage with interview and archive rhetoric: unstyled wardrobe light, mixed color temperatures, a zoom finding focus, and respect without a glamour rim. Fictional films may borrow the same grammar as mockumentary. That is still documentary rhetoric, not a recovered camcorder tape.

items.name: Blockbuster Gloss
items.prompt: Blockbuster gloss on [Subject], expensive contrast, clean skies, heroic rim, volumetric haze, IMAX-scale finish, adventure poster in motion. Name the rim and the horizon.
items.definition: Blockbuster cinematography is high-contrast, billboard-readable coverage: clean skies or designed weather, a heroic rim on hair and shoulder, volumetric shafts, and a grade that often splits teal shadow from warm skin. The shot must still parse at poster size.

items.name: Arthouse
items.prompt: Arthouse still of [Subject], patience, odd headroom, natural window light, the frame willing to be empty, static camera, duration implied. Name the unused air in the frame.
items.definition: Arthouse cinematography leaves space for thought: a static camera, odd headroom, natural or window light, and a frame willing to be empty. Duration is implied even in a still. The picture does not sell itself as a poster.

items.name: Animation
items.prompt: Animated treatment of [Subject], graphic volume, designed light, motion as drawing rather than photography. Name the medium (halftone, charcoal, cel, graphic CG).
items.definition: Animation cinematography constructs light and motion instead of capturing them: graphic volume, designed keys, and movement as drawing, paint, or stepped CG, not as a photographed exposure. The world is built. Lens physics appear only if you choose them.

items.name: BTS
items.prompt: Behind-the-scenes look at [Subject], crew, C-stands, and the set edge visible, the fiction leaking, worklight mixed with the scene key. Name a stand or a flag.
items.definition: Behind the scenes cinematography shows the making: C-stands, flags, the set wall, and crew in the same frame as the fiction, so the constructed world leaks. Documentary light (worklamps, mixed Kinos) sits beside the scene's key.

items.name: Dreamcore
items.prompt: Dreamcore image of [Subject], liminal rooms, soft fluorescent or blown window, childhood lighting gone wrong, low contrast, a memory that will not resolve. Name the empty hall or pool.
items.definition: The dreamcore aesthetic is a soft, liminal interior look: empty rooms, pools, and suburban halls lit by childhood practicals gone slightly wrong, with low contrast and unresolved space. Nostalgia is present. Safety is not.

items.name: Dystopian
items.prompt: Dystopian view of [Subject], civic scale gone cold, haze, signage, and rank, used surfaces, a future that already feels worn. Name the checkpoint, queue, or tower.
items.definition: Dystopian cinematography makes the civic system the antagonist: used architecture, haze, rank, and signage at a scale that already feels worn. The future is not shiny. It is bureaucratic, polluted, or monumental and cold, often in daylight as well as night.

items.name: Magical Realism
items.prompt: Magical-realist image of [Subject], ordinary window or overcast light, 35mm eye level, one impossible fact treated as weather, no extra rim, no dutch. Name the ordinary room and the single impossibility.
items.definition: Magical realism cinematography treats an extraordinary event as ordinary inside a recognizable world: the same window light, the same 35mm coverage, with one impossible fact staged as if it were weather. The camera does not gawk, add a rim, or warp the lens.

items.name: Maximalism
items.prompt: Maximalist frame of [Subject], too much color, too much pattern, multiple practicals, density as the point, 24mm to 40mm so the clutter stays readable. Name the wallpaper and the costume clash.
items.definition: Maximalist cinematography uses density as the point: too much color, too much pattern, ornament in every zone, and lighting that keeps the clutter readable rather than hiding it. Restraint would be a lie, so the frame is packed on purpose.

items.name: Photography
items.prompt: Still-photography grammar on [Subject], a single decisive frame, posed or window light, tripod, the movie pretending to be a print. Name the print logic (candle tableau, river still, posed portrait).
items.definition: Photographic cinematography treats the movie as a print: a single decisive frame, posed or found light, often centered composition or tableau blocking, with the camera pretending it could hang on a wall. Motion is allowed, but the still is the law.

items.name: Pixel Art
items.prompt: Lead with who does what. Camera, light, and style follow.
items.definition: Pixel art builds the image from visible tiles or a low-resolution grid. The world is discrete squares, not continuous grain.

items.name: Stylistic Suck
items.prompt: Deliberate amateur look on [Subject], hunting zoom, cheap video, wrong white balance as a choice, blown practicals, bad centering. Do not add a timestamp unless there is also a diegetic camera.
items.definition: Stylistic suck is deliberate amateur cinematography: hunting zooms, cheap video, and the wrong white balance as a choice of the film's own camera, not necessarily of a character's recovered tape. Polish would be dishonest, so the image is ugly on purpose.

items.name: Video Game
items.prompt: Video-game camera on [Subject], follow cam or isometric logic, HUD implied, space as a level, boom height locked, path readable. Name the camera type.
items.definition: Video game cinematography uses playable camera logic: a follow cam, an isometric view, or an FPS eyeline, with space readable as a level and a HUD implied. Collision, boom height, and pathing constrain the lens the way a game engine would.

items.name: Weirdcore
items.prompt: Weirdcore image of [Subject], early-web dread, low-res sacred, wrong crop, JPEG artifacts, a joke that is also a threat. Name the caption or the chopped face.
items.definition: The weirdcore aesthetic renders the familiar incorrectly: early-web compression, low-res sacred images, off-center crops, and a joke that is also a threat. The file looks like it should not have opened. Light is on-camera flash or a dim analog room, not a designed key.

items.name: Agamemnon
items.prompt: Lead with the person and the stand, then the grade. Example: Agamemnon look on [Subject], bronze, blood-dusk, tragic scale, a king under a bad sky, antique epic as grade.
items.definition: Agamemnon, the agamemnon look, is a named grade of hard sun, bronze bounce, and a dusk sky the color of a bruise, so a living body reads as antique metal. The name is not a shot: you still lock a height, pick a lens, and place a figure who can hold that weather.

items.name: Ink Riot
items.prompt: Hold a readable subject, then the liquid. Ink riot around [Subject], black and color blooming in liquid, calligraphy as explosion, a page that fights.
